intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 13 October 2026 was conducted in three shifts. Unofficial figures show that the first shift was perceived as ranging from easy to moderate, the second shift as moderate, and the third shift as moderate to difficult. Reported good attempt ranges are 20-84 for shift 1, 65-87 for shift 2, and 60-89 for shift 3, but these numbers are not official and SSC normalises scores across shifts. Candidates highlighted time pressure in the quantitative sections across all shifts. No further official analysis has been released.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level reported for each shift on 13 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 was described as ranging from easy to moderate, shift 2 was reported as moderate by most candidates, and shift 3 was seen as moderate to difficult.

faqs.q: How did candidates describe the quantitative section across the shifts on 13 October 2026?
faqs.a: In all three shifts, candidates noted that the quantitative section contained many advanced and calculative questions, leading to time pressure and making it the toughest part of the paper.

faqs.q: What are the unofficial good attempt ranges for the shifts on 13 October 2026?
faqs.a: The unofficial good attempt ranges are 20-84 for shift 1, 65-87 for shift 2, and 60-89 for shift 3. These figures are not official and are provided only for reference.

faqs.q: Did candidates report any time‑management issues on 13 October 2026?
faqs.a: Yes, candidates across the shifts reported time‑management concerns, especially in the quantitative section and the English reading passage.

faqs.q: How does SSC handle score normalization across the shifts on 13 October 2026?
faqs.a: SSC normalises scores across shifts to ensure comparability, but the exact methodology is not publicly disclosed.
